sentences.text: 2. Heard Sri Javeed S., learned counsel for the petitioner and Smt. Waheedha M.M., learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent- State.
Perused the materials on record.

3. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the petitioner is entitled for grant of bail under Section 438 of Cr.P.C.?"
NC: 2024:KHC:18872

My answer to the above point is in 'Affirmative' for the following:
REASONS 4. Petitioner- accused No.1 is before this Court seeking grant of anticipatory bail on the ground that he is having apprehension of being arrested.
The wife of the petitioner lodged first information on 02.01.2024 against the petitioner as well as his brother and mother.
Both of them were apprehended and released on bail.
It is stated that the petitioner had married the informant during 2014.
It is alleged that the petitioner demanded dowry at the time of marriage and also subsequently.
Even according to the informant, she had been to Saudi Arabia along with the petitioner some time after the marriage.
The informant alleged that accused No.1 ill-treated her at the instance of accused Nos.2 and 3 and deserted her.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is the permanent resident of the address mentioned in the petition and he will abide by any of the conditions that will be imposed by this Court.
Admittedly, the complainant has NC: 2024:KHC:18872 not sustained any injury and the main allegation is that accused No.1 had deserted her.
Admittedly, the petitioner is not required for interrogation.

Considering all these facts and circumstances, I am of the opinion that petitioner has made out prima-facie case of apprehension of arrest in the criminal case registered on the basis of the complaint lodged by the wife of the petitioner.

Hence, I am of the opinion that the petitioner may be granted anticipatory bail subject to conditions, which will take care of the apprehension expressed by the learned High Court Government Pleader that the petitioner may abscond or may tamper or threaten the prosecution witnesses.

sentences.text:
Accordingly, I answer the above point in the affirmative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed.
The petitioner is ordered to be enlarged on bail in the event of his arrest in Crime No.2/2024 of Kundapura Police Station.

The petitioner is directed to appear before the Investigating Officer within 15 days from the date of receipt of NC: 2024:KHC:18872 this order and on his appearance,
the Investigating Officer shall enlarge him on bail subject to the following conditions:-
a.

The petitioner shall furnish the bond in a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lakhs only) with two sureties for the likesum to the satisfaction of the Investigating Officer; b. The petitioner shall not commit any offence against the wife of the petitioner or her family members; and c.
The petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer or the Court as and when required.
On furnishing the sureties by the petitioner, the Investigating Officer is at liberty to verify the correctness of the address and authenticity of the documents furnished by him.
On satisfaction of the said documents, he may proceed to accept the sureties within a reasonable time.
